# planetscale_postgres_branch_maintenance_window (Resource)

PostgresBranchMaintenanceWindow Resource

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "planetscale_postgres_branch_maintenance_window" "main" {
  organization = "my-organization"
  database     = "my-database"
  branch       = "main"

  # Sundays at 03:00 UTC
  day  = 0
  hour = 3
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `branch` (String) Branch name from `list_branches`. Example: `main`. Requires replacement if changed.
- `database` (String) Database name slug from `list_databases`. Example: `app-db`. Requires replacement if changed.
- `day` (Number) Day of the week the window opens, in UTC, from 0 (Sunday) to 6 (Saturday).
- `hour` (Number) Hour of the day the window opens, in UTC, from 0 to 23.
- `organization` (String) Organization name slug from `list_organizations`. Example: `acme`. Requires replacement if changed.

### Read-Only

- `duration` (Number) The duration of the maintenance window in hours
- `id` (String) The ID of the maintenance schedule

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = planetscale_postgres_branch_maintenance_window.my_planetscale_postgres_branch_maintenance_window
  id = jsonencode({
    branch       = "..."
    database     = "..."
    organization = "..."
  })
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import planetscale_postgres_branch_maintenance_window.my_planetscale_postgres_branch_maintenance_window '{"branch": "...", "database": "...", "organization": "..."}'
```
